note: `expect` is the WC-* code a conforming verifier must produce; null means the contract must be admitted. `stage` is `artifact` for checks a verifier can make from the artifact and a trusted key alone, and `context` for checks needing an authenticated peer, a presented surface, a revocation feed or zone policy — a command-line verifier must ADMIT those and a mediator must refuse them.
scenario_note: A mediator scenario carries the context an artifact-only verifier does not have: an authenticated peer pair, the surface the callee presented, a revocation feed and local zone policy. `expect` is "admit" or the WC-* code a conforming MEDIATOR must return. These are what makes the four context-stage vectors checkable instead of deferred.

peer-mismatch.json.description: A valid contract presented for a caller it does not name.
peer-mismatch.json.rule: The check the whole two-plane design rests on: identity is AUTHENTICATED and compared to the contract's claim, never taken from the claim. Uses the valid artifact deliberately — the artifact is not the thing that is wrong.

posture-unattested.json.description: A valid artifact whose counterparty is not attested.
posture-unattested.json.rule: Posture is carried in the artifact and enforced by the mediator, not by the issuer. In enforce mode an unattested counterparty is refused; in observe it becomes a finding.

revoked-jti.json.description: The artifact id is on the revocation feed.
revoked-jti.json.rule: Revocation is consulted at admission, so a contract that verified a moment ago stops verifying the moment the feed says so — no cache rebuild.

surface-superset.json.description: The contract claims a tool the callee does not present.
surface-superset.json.rule: The pin is compared over the contracted subset, so an additive tool outside the contract is benign and a contracted item that is absent or changed is always drift. Paths in a scenario resolve relative to the scenario file.

valid-es256.json.description: The positive control: every context check satisfied.
valid-es256.json.rule: A conformance set of refusals alone is passed by an implementation that refuses everything. This is the vector that makes the other five mean something.

zone-crossing.json.description: internal to partner with no local rule permitting it.
zone-crossing.json.rule: Zone policy is the mediator's, not the contract's. A signed contract cannot open a crossing local policy has not declared.

alg-confusion-ed-for-es.jws.description: EdDSA signature under a kid registered for ES256

aud-other-mediator.jws.description: addressed to a different mediator; replay must fail

expired.jws.description: exp in the past; no grace period

hmac-hs256.jws.description: HMAC: anyone who can verify could also mint

no-kid.jws.description: no kid, so no key can be resolved

posture-unattested.jws.description: artifact is valid; admission denies on posture in enforce mode

revoked-jti.jws.description: artifact id on the revocation feed

schema-99.jws.description: a newer payload schema; reject rather than guess

surface-superset.jws.description: surface widened and re-signed; the digest no longer matches

unknown-claim.jws.description: an unrecognised claim a verifier must not ignore

unknown-kid.jws.description: signed by a key the verifier does not trust

valid-ed25519.jws.description: the same contract signed with EdDSA

wrong-typ.jws.description: a JWT that is not a connection contract

zone-crossing.jws.description: internal to partner without an explicit rule
